summary: Wasco County, OR site on the Warm Springs Reservation; 1925 letters weighed it against Bald Peter, an unknown-type lookout is dated 1933, and it is gone. No source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: The register and firelookout.com both list the lookout as gone; no source describes what remains at the site
facts.agency: Warm Springs Indian Reservation (administrator per the register)

events.note: April 24, 1925 letter answers recommendations by F.W. Wilkes and William Heritage for a tower and cabin on Mutton Mountain in preference to Bald Peter, and favors Bald Peter; a May 13, 1925 Bend Bulletin item, quoted on the same page, reports the tower to be erected that season on Bald Peter
Lookout of unknown type built, per both lists
Registered August 26, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

notes_for_editor: Only the register and firelookout.com record a 1933 lookout on Mutton Mountain, and neither names a builder or design beyond unknown type. The only Mutton-specific history is the 1925 letter debate: Wilkes and Heritage recommended Mutton Mountain, the April 24 letter objected and favored Bald Peter, and a May 13 Bend Bulletin item reported a tower to be erected on Bald Peter that season. The sources do not connect that to the 1933 structure. Brief access 'permission' is not stated by any source read, so access is left out of facts. Not used: a 2,424-acre fire 15 miles northeast of Warm Springs, east of the Mutton Mountains, reported Friday August 28 (1981 newspaper page at oregonnews.uoregon.edu, PDF seq-11). It names the area but no lookout, so it is left out of the story. A Washington lookout called Mutton Mountain (washingtonlookouts.weebly.com) appeared in search; it is a different site and was not used.
